text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
Citizenship(x, y) ::: x has citizenship y.
HoldOfficial(x, y) ::: x holds the official position y.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
RussianFederation(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Taiwanese(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
USCitizenship(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina
Gazprom ::: Gazprom
Year(2024) ::: the year 2024

Premises:
∀x (USCitizenship(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: Anyone with U.S. citizenship can register to vote.
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Anyone who can register can participate in the election.
∀x (Citizenship(x, US) ∨ Citizenship(x, Taiwan)) ::: Everyone has either U.S. or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (HoldOfficial(x, RussianFederation) ∧ Taiwanese(x)) ::: No Russian Federation official holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir ∧ ¬Citizenship(Vladimir, Taiwan) ∧ ¬Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is a manager at Gazprom.
Ekaterina ∧ (CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ HoldOfficial(Ekaterina, RussianFederation)) ::: Ekaterina can either register to vote or is a Russian Federation official.

Conclusion:
¬HoldOfficial(Vladimir, RussianFederation) ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official.
